title: Loan Repayment, EMI Auto-Debit and Foreclosure Policy
content: Loan EMIs are auto-debited from the linked repayment account via NACH mandate on the scheduled due date each month. Customers wishing to view repayment schedules, download interest certificates, check foreclosure charges, or obtain a No Objection Certificate after full repayment can access Loan Services in Mobile Banking or NetBanking, or request specialist assistance for restructuring. Floating rate personal loans and home loans to individual borrowers have zero foreclosure penalty.

title: Personal Loans Eligibility, Interest Rates, and Instant Disbursal
content: Personal loans are collateral-free unsecured loans available for salaried and self-employed professionals with a minimum net monthly income of ₹25,000. Loan amounts range from ₹50,000 to ₹40,00,000 with flexible tenures of 12 to 60 months. Interest rates range from 10.50% to 16.00% p.a. based on credit score. Pre-approved customers can receive instant 100% digital disbursal within 10 minutes via Account Aggregator verification on the mobile app.

title: Home Loan Features, LTV Ratio, and Repo-Linked Benchmark (RLLR)
content: Home loans are offered for purchase, construction, or plot purchase with attractive floating interest rates linked to the RBI Repo Linked Lending Rate (RLLR). Loan to Value (LTV) limits: Up to 90% for property values up to ₹30 Lakhs; up to 80% for values between ₹30L and ₹75L; up to 75% for values above ₹75L. Repayment tenures extend up to 30 years or age 70 at maturity.

title: Income Tax Deductions on Home Loans (Section 80C and Section 24b)
content: Home loan borrowers are eligible for significant tax deductions: Section 80C allows a deduction of up to ₹1,50,000 on principal repayment. Section 24(b) permits a deduction of up to ₹2,00,000 on interest paid for self-occupied properties. Joint owners can both claim these individual deductions separately. Provisional and final interest certificates can be downloaded in PDF from Mobile Banking under Loan Accounts.

title: Vehicle and Car Loans Financing and Hypothecation Removal (Form 35)
content: Car loans cover up to 90% of on-road vehicle cost for tenures up to 7 years with competitive fixed or floating interest rates. The vehicle Registration Certificate (RC) carries a hypothecation endorsement in favor of the bank. Upon final EMI repayment, the bank issues a No Objection Certificate (NOC) and duplicate Form 35 within 14 days, allowing the owner to remove the bank lien at the regional RTO.

title: Gold Loans Against Jewelry, LTV Cap, and Bullet Repayment
content: Instant gold loans are sanctioned against 18-karat to 24-karat gold jewelry with same-day cash or account disbursal. In accordance with RBI guidelines, the maximum Loan to Value (LTV) is capped at 75% of the net gold market valuation. Repayment options include regular monthly EMI or Bullet Repayment (where both principal and accrued interest are paid in a single lump sum at the end of the 12-month tenure). Jewelry is insured and held in high-security bank vaults.

title: Education Loans for Domestic and Overseas Studies and Moratorium
content: Education loans provide funding up to ₹7.5 Lakhs without any tangible collateral, and up to ₹1.5 Crores with collateral for premier institutions and overseas studies. The loan covers tuition fees, accommodation, books, and travel. A repayment moratorium applies for the full course duration plus 1 year or 6 months after securing employment. Interest paid on education loans qualifies for 100% tax deduction under Section 80E without upper limit for 8 years.

title: RBI Zero Foreclosure Charges Mandate on Floating Rate Loans
content: Under RBI circular directives, banks and NBFCs are strictly prohibited from charging any foreclosure fees, pre-payment penalties, or exit loads on floating rate term loans sanctioned to individual borrowers (with or without co-obligants). Borrowers can make partial prepayments or close their loan ahead of tenure at any time with zero penalty. Fixed rate commercial business loans may attract a prepayment charge of 2% to 3% plus GST.

title: Release of Original Property Title Deeds and ₹5,000/Day Delay Compensation
content: Under RBI Master Direction issued in 2023, regulated entities must release all original movable/immovable property documents and remove charges registered with CERSAI within 30 calendar days of full loan repayment. If the bank fails to return original documents within 30 days, it must compensate the borrower at ₹5,000 for each day of delay. In case of lost documents, the bank must obtain certified duplicates at its own cost plus pay compensation.

title: EMI NACH Bounce Charges, Grace Period, and Credit Score Impact
content: If a loan EMI fails due to insufficient funds during NACH auto-debit, a bounce penalty of ₹450 to ₹500 plus GST is levied. A secondary debit representation is attempted 5 days later. Any EMI overdue beyond 30 days is reported to credit bureaus (CIBIL, Experian, CRIF High Mark), which can lower the borrower's credit score by 40 to 60 points and impair future loan eligibility. Borrowers should maintain sufficient balance 1 day prior to the debit date.

title: CIBIL Credit Score Optimization and Dispute Rectification
content: Credit scores range from 300 to 900. A score of 750 or higher qualifies for preferential interest rate discounts. Factors influencing score: Repayment track record (35%), credit utilization ratio kept under 30% (30%), age of credit history (15%), healthy mix of secured and unsecured credit (10%), and low hard inquiries (10%). If an incorrect overdue is shown, customers can raise a free dispute on CIBIL or contact the bank nodal officer.

title: Top-Up Home Loans for Renovation, Business, and Higher Education
content: Existing home loan borrowers who have maintained an unblemished repayment track record for at least 12 months can avail of a Top-Up Home Loan. The top-up amount can be used for home renovation, furniture purchase, children's marriage, or medical contingencies. It carries the same low interest rate as the primary home loan and can be amortized over the remaining tenure of the parent loan.

title: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) Credit Linked Subsidy Guidelines
content: Under the government PMAY scheme, eligible first-time home buyers in Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Low Income Groups (LIG), and Middle Income Groups (MIG) receive interest subsidies up to ₹2.67 Lakhs on housing loans. The subsidy amount is credited upfront to the borrower's loan account by the National Housing Bank (NHB), reducing the effective principal and monthly EMI.

title: Loan Tenure Extension and Restructuring for Financial Hardship
content: Borrowers encountering genuine financial emergencies, job loss, or illness can apply for loan restructuring or tenure extension to lower their monthly EMI obligation. Requests can be submitted at the home branch with supporting medical or employment evidence. Extending tenure increases the total interest over the life of the loan but provides immediate cash flow relief.

title: Loan Account Closure, No Dues Certificate (NDC), and Statement Retrieval
content: Once the final EMI is settled, a digital No Dues Certificate (NDC) or No Objection Certificate (NOC) is generated automatically within 48 hours and can be downloaded from NetBanking. Physical NOC and closure letters are dispatched via registered speed post to the registered communication address within 7 working days. Comprehensive loan amortization statements are permanently accessible in the app.
